newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi troops kill 10 Hutu rebels, army says.
newsitem.headline: Burundi troops kill 10 Hutu rebels, army says.

text.p: Burundi's army said on Tuesday its troops killed 10 Hutu rebels in a week-long offensive in the Kibira forest in the north and called on other rebels to surrender.
One soldier was killed in the offensive launched on January 15, said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi.

"This is an appeal to people sympathetic to the rebels but also to the rebels themselves," Nibizi added. "If they surrender we will not harm them but if they do not we will continue to attack and we will destroy them."
Nibizi said the army killed 10 rebels in Kibira forest, seen by the Tutsi-dominated military as the main rebel stronghold in Burundi. No independent confirmation was available.
Hundreds of Hutu rebels, mainly from the National Council for the Defence of Democracy, moved into the forest last October after they were forced from bases in refugee camps in eastern Zaire.
Nibizi said the army blocked paths and sent soldiers on foot into the forest, which is dense and has a triple canopy of vegetation. The forest stretches north into neighbouring Rwanda.
The army attempted last November to penetrate the forest, said by witnesses to contain a series of rebel training camps and a Hutu administration opposed to the Burundi government.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi's civil war and massacres since October 1993 when the country's first Hutu president was murdered in an attempted army coup.
